dish: Hakodate shio ramen (Ajisai shio — kelp-clear broth)
n: Ajisai Honten, Hakodate (函館麺厨房あじさい 本店)
w: Founded 1930, the name in Hakodate shio ramen: a clear broth of southern-Dōnan kelp with pork and chicken bone and rock salt. Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100.

n: Lucky Pierrot Bay Area Honten (ラッキーピエロ ベイエリア本店)
address: Bay Area waterfront, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Hakodate's own clown-themed burger chain (17 branches, all in the city) — the Chinese Chicken Burger, curry rice and soft-serve; the waterfront flagship.

dish: Asahikawa shōyu ramen (oily-sealed double broth, thin wavy noodles)
n: Asahikawa Ramen Village (あさひかわラーメン村)
w: Eight of Asahikawa's best-known shops under one roof — the city's shōyu style: pork-bone and seafood double broth sealed under a film of lard, thin, firm, wavy noodles.

n: Ganso Butadon no Panchō, Obihiro (元祖豚丼のぱんちょう)
address: In front of Obihiro Station, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The 1933 Obihiro shop credited with inventing butadon — sweet-soy charcoal-grilled pork on rice, the Tokachi soul food. The name is from the Chinese 'fan ting'.

n: Butadon no Tonta, Obihiro (ぶた丼のとん田)
w: Among Obihiro's most popular butadon counters; Michelin Bib Gourmand in the Hokkaido 2017 special edition.
Otaru's Michelin-starred sushi counter (Hokkaido guide one star), with a casual by-the-piece outpost inside Otaru Station.
